## Chapter 18

# Machine Learning for Financial Data Forecasting:

## Deep Learning-Powered Scientometric Analysis

Imane Boudri

[![Orcid Image](image/orcid-logo.png)https://orcid.org/0009-0007-5163-108X](https://orcid.org/0009-0007-5163-108X)

Institut Supérieur de Commerce et d'Administration des Entreprises, Morocco

Zineb Sabri

Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University, Morocco

### ABSTRACT

Recent studies underscore the growing application of machine learning (ML) in finance, as revealed through bibliometric analyses. Kureljusic and Karger (2024) reviewed AI-based forecasting in financial accounting, identifying gaps and proposing future research agendas. Similarly, Biju et al. (2023) explored the taxonomy of AI, deep learning, and ML in finance, highlighting the rise in publications and the need for empirical studies on algorithmic financial technologies. Building on this foundation, this study presents a scientometric analysis of ML in financial data forecasting from 1996 to 2024. Using data from Scopus and Web of Science, we examine key themes, collaboration networks, and influential contributors. Employing deep learning tools like Sentence-BERT, BerTopic, BERT, ChatGPT, and PEGASUS, we offer insights into how ML has reshaped financial forecasting. This analysis provides a basis for future research, guiding scholars and practitioners towards impactful areas in finance.

### 1\. INTRODUCTION

The growing demand to quantify research output has given rise to scientometric and bibliometric studies that map the progression of scientific fields. Science can be understood as a self-organizing system driven by informational flows, where new discoveries build upon past ideas, evolving through a collective and sequential process. While external factors such as societal pressures and organizational structures may influence the environment in which science operates, they do not fundamentally alter its organic direction—similar to how an organism’s development is shaped by hereditary information rather than external conditions ([Nalimov & Mulchenko, 1971](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1119)). In the context of financial data forecasting, the integration of machine learning techniques represents a significant evolution, driven by the potential of these technologies to transform predictive modeling, risk assessment, and decision-making processes.

Motivated by the intersection of scientometric analysis and the transformative potential of machine learning in finance, this chapter seeks to address several key questions: What are the primary themes and collaboration networks shaping this field? How have influential contributors and research clusters evolved over time? What gaps exist in the current literature that could inspire future innovation? By answering these questions, we aim to highlight the critical role of scientometric tools in uncovering hidden patterns and fostering interdisciplinary collaborations.

Conducting a scientometric study in the field of machine learning for financial forecasting provides essential insights into the development of research methodologies and highlights the contributions of influential authors. These analyses serve as a roadmap to understand the research landscape by identifying emerging themes through keyword co-occurrence, revealing trends that can shape future research ([Donthu et al., 2021](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1102)). Furthermore, scientometrics play a crucial role in revealing collaboration networks among researchers, highlighting partnerships that drive innovation across various scientific domains. By mapping the collaborative and thematic dimensions of a field, these studies provide insights into the pathways through which knowledge evolves, enabling scholars to identify emerging trends, influential authors, and significant research clusters. Scientometrics also help uncover interdisciplinary linkages, showcasing how different fields converge to tackle complex challenges and fostering a more integrated research community. This approach not only informs future research directions but also enhances the collective understanding of scientific advancements and their broader implications.

Recent studies highlight the growing application of machine learning in finance, as illustrated through comprehensive bibliometric analyses. For example, [Kureljusic and Karger (2024)](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1112) systematically reviewed AI-based forecasting in financial accounting, identifying gaps and proposing future research agendas. Similarly, Biju et al. (2023) examined the taxonomy of artificial intelligence, deep learning, and machine learning in finance, revealing a surge in publication trends and the need for empirical research on algorithmic financial technologies. These findings collectively emphasize the critical role of bibliometric and scientometric studies in mapping the landscape of machine learning applications in finance, underscoring the importance of understanding not only the current trends but also the foundational partnerships and methodologies driving the field forward.

This study builds upon this body of work by presenting a scientometric analysis of machine learning for financial data forecasting from 1996 to 2024. Using data from Scopus and Web of Science, this study explores the primary themes, collaboration networks, and influential contributors in this field. By leveraging deep learning tools such as embedding vectors, topic modeling, and text summarization, powered by models like Sentence-BERT, BerTopic, BERT, ChatGPT, and PEGASUS, we aim to provide a nuanced understanding of how machine learning has reshaped financial forecasting. Ultimately, this analysis offers a foundation for future research, guiding scholars, practitioners, and policymakers towards areas with the potential for significant impact in finance.

### 2\. LITERATURE REVIEW

Bibliometric analysis is a widely recognized and rigorous method for exploring and analyzing large volumes of scientific data ([Donthu et al., 2021](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1102)). More specifically, a Bibliometric analysis refers to the quantitative study of bibliographic material. It involves measuring and analyzing various aspects of scientific publications, such as the number of papers, citations, authors, and journals, in order to provide a comprehensive overview of a research field ([Merigó & Yang, 2017](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1117)). This approach allows for the classification and ranking of publications, authors, and sources, which helps to identify influential works and key contributors within a specific domain.

Building on this, bibliometric analysis not only offers a general picture of a research field but also unveils the subtle evolutionary trends within it, while highlighting emerging areas of interest. By shedding light on both established and growing research trajectories, bibliometric analysis becomes an essential tool for understanding the dynamic development of scientific knowledge.

Thus, researchers may eventually delineate the boundary between what is known and what remains unknown, allowing them to more effectively identify gaps in the current understanding of a field. This distinction is crucial for guiding future research efforts, as it highlights areas that require further investigation and fosters innovation by encouraging scholars to explore uncharted territories. By clearly delineating what is known from what remains uncertain, researchers can prioritize their inquiries, allocate resources more effectively, and contribute to the advancement of scientific discovery, particularly in rapidly evolving fields like data science ([Purnomo et al., 2020](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1123)) and artificial intelligence ([Tapeh & Naser, 2023](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1127)).

However, in our work, we have opted to use the terms “scientometric analysis” and “scientometrics”, as they better reflect the specific context of our study, which is centered on the assessment of scientific outputs, research performance, and the structure of knowledge within a defined scientific field. And which also focuses on the quantitative evaluation of the dynamics of scientific production and research ([Ellegaard & Wallin, 2015](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1103); [Bar-Ilan 2008](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1092), [2010](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1093)). Historically, scientometrics originated as a method to quantify communication processes within science, formally defined by [Nalimov and Mulchenko (1971)](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1119) as the study of quantitative methods analyzing the development of science as an informational process. Its scope has since expanded, incorporating sub-disciplines like bibliometrics, informetrics, webometrics, and altmetrics, which address digital and social media impacts on scientific communication ([Mingers & Leydesdorff, 2015](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1118)).

The development of scientometrics has primarily focused on citation analysis, which creates links between researchers, ideas, publications, and institutions, allowing for the empirical study of scientific networks ([Mingers & Leydesdorff, 2015](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1118); [De Bellis, 2014](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1100)). Initiated by Eugene Garfield with the creation of the Science Citation Index (SCI) in the 1950s, this field evolved to include various metrics, such as the impact factor for evaluating journals, and co-citation networks to map relationships between publications (Larsen & Ins, 2010; [Carpenter & Narin, 1981](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1096)). The SCI, now part of the Web of Science, has enabled numerous advancements, including visualizing scientific networks and the analysis of scholar productivity with concepts like the h-index, considered one of the next-generation metrics and indicators ([Dong et al., 2015](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1101); [Hirsch & Buela-Casal, 2014](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1107); [Kelly & Jennions, 2006](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1109); [Hirsch, 2005](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1106)). Though impactful, traditional metrics face limitations, such as biases introduced by hyperauthorship or varying citation practices. Metrics like h-frac offer alternatives addressing these challenges, reflecting more accurate scholarly contributions (Singhal et al., 2013; [Koltun & Hafner, 2021](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1110)).

Additionally, keyword co-occurrence analysis is widely applied to understand thematic trends by analyzing the co-occurrence of keywords in titles, abstracts, or full texts ([Zhao, 2024](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1138); [Narong & Hallinger, 2023](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1121); Bornmann et al., 2017). Network analysis techniques are frequently utilized to visualize the connections between authors, institutions, or topics, enhancing the understanding of collaboration and knowledge flow ([Yue et al., 2021](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1132); [Madani, 2015](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1114)).

These methods, often combined with data visualization tools such as VOSviewer, Gephi, and R (via packages like bibliometrix, ggplot2, igraph or biblioshiny), are integral in uncovering the dynamics of scientific knowledge production and identifying emerging research frontiers ([Purnomo et al., 2020](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1123)). R has become a powerful tool in the field, offering robust statistical and visualization capabilities, making it highly versatile for bibliometric and scientometric analyses ([Zejjari & Benhayoun, 2024](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1134)).

In recent years, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into scientometric analysis has opened new avenues for more advanced and nuanced insights. AI-powered tools can process large datasets far beyond human capacity, facilitating real-time tracking of scientific trends and the detection of intricate patterns across disciplines. Machine learning algorithms, for instance, enhance traditional citation analysis by identifying latent relationships between publications, authors, and institutions that may not be immediately apparent through manual methods. Natural language processing (NLP) further broadens the analytical scope by examining the textual content of research articles, enabling sentiment analysis, keyword extraction, and thematic clustering ([Gomez et al., 2023](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1104); Bertin & Atanassova, 2018). Furthermore, the integration of AI in scientometric studies remains a niche topic that continues to gain traction due to its potential to revolutionize research analytics. The novelty of this approach lies in its ability to uncover hidden patterns and trends, making it highly relevant for the current era of data-driven decision-making in academia and industry.

Recent studies emphasize the transformative role of advanced machine learning models in enhancing scientometric and bibliometric analyses. [Daradkeh et al. (2022)](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1099) demonstrated how convolutional neural networks (CNNs) improve the classification and visualization of research data, addressing the limitations of traditional bibliometric methods in handling complex datasets. Similarly, [Boujija & Pradier (2024)](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1094) utilized BERTopic to conduct a multilingual bibliometric analysis, highlighting its capacity for nuanced theme detection and overcoming keyword-based analysis limitations. [Wolff et al. (2024)](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1130) further showcased the efficiency of pre-trained models like SciBERT and SPECTER2, enriched with metadata from databases such as OpenAlex, in enabling fine-grained scholarly classification and adapting to evolving research taxonomies. Collectively, these studies illustrate how machine learning techniques bridge gaps in traditional scientometric approaches, paving the way for refined mappings of research landscapes.

The application of machine learning techniques in financial forecasting emerges from the need to address complex, data-intensive challenges inherent to the financial sector. Unlike its role in scientometric research, where ML enhances the analysis of scholarly outputs, its use in financial forecasting is motivated by the demand for accurate predictions of market trends, risk assessment, and decision-making (Wasserbacher & Spondler, 2022)

In this sense, ML techniques have revolutionized financial data forecasting by introducing sophisticated tools to analyze and predict market behavior. Techniques like regression analysis, decision trees, support vector machines (SVM), and deep learning have been successfully applied to predict market trends and stock prices ([Olubusola et al., 2024](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1122)). Deep learning and reinforcement learning excel in processing complex datasets, boosting prediction precision ([Nandi et al., 2023](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1120)). Hybrid models combining multiple ML techniques further improve forecasting accuracy ([Chen et al., 2019](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1097); [Henrique et al., 2019](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1105)).

Recent bibliometric and scientometric analyses have shed light on the growing intersection of machine learning and financial data forecasting. For instance, [Zakaria et al. (2023)](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1133) conducted a comprehensive bibliometric study analyzing 189 articles from SCOPUS, revealing a notable increase in publications post-2017. Their findings highlighted key trends in the application of machine learning technologies for various financial forecasting tasks, such as crowdfunding and bankruptcy prediction. Similarly, [Salehpour & Samadzamini (2024)](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1124) explored machine learning applications within economics, econometrics and finance, analyzing publications from 2013 to 2022. Their research provided insights into how machine learning is increasingly integrated into economic forecasting models, thus enhancing predictive accuracy in this domain.

Along the same lines, [Manogna & Anand (2023)](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1115) provide a comprehensive analysis of the impact of prominent authors in the field of finance, particularly focusing on the application of deep learning (DL). The findings highlight a significant increase in the use of DL in finance since 2017. Four key research areas are identified: neural networks and stock market simulations, portfolio optimization and risk management, time series analysis and forecasting, and high-frequency trading.

Moreover, [Martins & Galegale (2023)](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1116) focused on a broader bibliometric analysis of machine learning literature, emphasizing predictive algorithms relevant to financial data forecasting. They identified key themes and citation trends while pointing out the lack of consolidated studies linking machine learning with big data in finance. Collectively, these studies underscore the importance of bibliometric and scientometric analyses in mapping the evolving landscape of machine learning applications in finance, revealing influential researchers and highlighting areas for future research exploration.

### 3\. MATERIAL AND METHODS

To achieve the objectives of this chapter, we adopted a connectionist approach for conducting a scientometric analysis on the application of machine learning in financial time series forecasting. This approach aims to capture intricate relationships and patterns within large datasets, enhancing our understanding of how machine learning, particularly deep learning models, has been utilized in forecasting financial trends. The methodology provides a nuanced analysis of the existing research landscape while identifying emerging trends and areas for future exploration.

#### 3.1 Data Collection

Data for this study were sourced from Scopus and Web of Science using structured queries with keywords such as “Machine Learning,” “Financial Data,” and “Forecasting.” After removing duplicates, a total of 892 unique documents, published between 1996 and 2024, were compiled. Metadata, including author affiliations, keywords, abstracts, and citation counts, formed the basis of the analysis. Documents in various languages were retained to ensure comprehensive coverage, while English dominated the dataset.

#### 3.2 Data Preprocessing

The raw metadata was unified into a consistent dataset. Duplicate entries were removed, and discrepancies between data entries from different databases were reconciled. Articles with available abstracts were prioritized to ensure the relevance and quality of the analysis. This preprocessing step enabled seamless integration with advanced analysis tools.

#### 3.3 Statistical and Network Analyses

Statistical methods assessed the productivity and impact of authors, institutions, and sources. Key metrics included the h-index, citation counts, and collaboration indices, which highlighted influential contributors and partnerships. Citation analysis mapped the growth of publications over time and identified shifts in research focus. Visualization techniques, such as Evolution Plots, tracked document production trends and keyword usage, offering insights into emerging themes within the domain.

Collaboration analysis examined co-authorship patterns at institutional and international levels. Global collaboration networks displayed the volume and intensity of research partnerships between institutions and countries, emphasizing the interdisciplinary and global nature of financial forecasting research.

#### 3.4 Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

To implement this approach, we employed the methodology proposed by Pereira et al. (2024). Their methodology introduces pyBibX, a Python library specifically designed to perform comprehensive bibliometric and scientometric analyses on raw data files sourced from databases like Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed. The core of this library integrates advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities, making it a powerful tool for conducting in-depth analyses. The methodology involves conducting a thorough Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), utilizing clear graphical presentations to examine the data’s structure, distributions, and potential anomalies. This step is followed by a network analysis that incorporates citation, collaboration, and similarity analysis, enabling us to uncover relationships between authors, institutions, and research topics. By examining these networks, we gain insights into the collaborative nature of the field, highlighting key contributors and influential partnerships.

Visualization techniques, such as word clouds, N-grams, and UMAP for dimensionality reduction, were employed using the pyBibX Python library. UMAP clusters documents based on semantic similarity, enabling an exploration of latent relationships within the dataset. Sankey diagrams illustrated the flow of research productivity across authors, institutions, and countries, while tree maps and bar plots quantified the distribution of research outputs.

#### 3.5 AI-Powered Analytical Tools

Advanced AI models were employed to enrich the analysis:

*   • BERT: Facilitated keyword extraction and semantic analysis for accurate classification of research themes.
    
*   • Sentence\-BERT: Generated embeddings for similarity analysis, clustering documents with thematic overlaps.
    
*   • BerTopic: Identified and categorized research themes, mapping trends and shifts over time.
    
*   • ChatGPT: Summarized large volumes of text, offering concise insights into research contributions.
    
*   • PEGASUS: Highlighted core ideas in documents through abstractive summarization.
    

These tools addressed challenges like data homogeneity and scalability, enabling a comprehensive and detailed scientometric analysis.

#### 3.6 Topic Modeling

Using embeddings from Sentence-BERT, topic modeling revealed thematic clusters and emerging research areas. Abstractive and extractive summarization techniques provided concise overviews of individual studies, highlighting their key contributions. This NLP-driven approach enriched the analysis, uncovering subtle connections between research themes and their evolution over time.

These insights deepen our understanding of how machine learning techniques are applied in financial data forecasting and reveal evolving interests within the field.

Additionally, the dataset reveals a total of 2219 authors’ keywords and 2056 Keywords Plus, which enhance the thematic breadth of the collection. The impact of these documents is illustrated by a total citation count of 16090, with an average of 5.73 citations per author and 18.04 citations per document. These metrics highlight the substantial engagement of the research community with this body of work, indicating that these publications are not only well-referenced but also influential in the field.

### 5\. DISCUSSION

This study provides a comprehensive scientometric analysis of the field of machine learning as applied to financial data forecasting, spanning from 1996 to 2024\. The documents analyzed in this research, totaling 892, were sourced exclusively from two prominent academic databases: Scopus and Web of Science. Our exploration into this body of literature has underscored the growing significance of machine learning techniques in finance, revealing an intensified interest in the field and the increasingly essential role that advanced algorithms play in shaping the future of financial analysis and prediction. This section synthesizes our findings, emphasizing the implications for researchers, investors, and regulators, while discussing the limitations of the study and suggesting avenues for future research.

Our analysis began with a general overview of the data, revealing that the number of published documents has grown substantially over the last decade, particularly since 2017. This expansion reflects an increasing recognition of the power of machine learning to provide robust financial forecasts, which are critical for both academic research and industry applications. Notably, a small cohort of authors emerged as leaders in this field, contributing a significant number of publications and establishing themselves as authorities. The productivity and sustained contributions of these individuals highlight the commitment and expertise they bring to financial forecasting through machine learning. This finding is complemented by the strong collaborative networks we observed globally, with intensive international partnerships between institutions. The prevalence of cross-border collaboration, particularly between researchers in the United States, Europe, and Asia, suggests a shared global interest in leveraging machine learning to enhance the predictive accuracy and efficiency of financial forecasts.

The thematic analysis we conducted further elucidates the specific areas of interest within this growing field. Our examination of common keywords and phrases revealed that “financial data processing”, “time series forecasting”, and “machine learning models” are among the most frequently studied topics. This focus indicates that researchers are particularly interested in developing methods for analyzing and forecasting time-series data, an essential component of financial markets. Additionally, the prominent appearance of terms like “LSTM” highlights a strong preference for artificial neural networks in general and the architecture of Long Short-Term Memory networks mostly, which have demonstrated their superiority in managing the sequential nature of financial data. LSTM models, specifically designed to capture long-term dependencies, have proven highly effective at uncovering temporal patterns in complex datasets. This aligns with the findings of other researchers who have consistently shown LSTM's effectiveness in financial forecasting tasks, especially stock market prediction ([Zhang et al., 2024](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1135); [Hu et al., 2021](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1108); [Kumar et al., 2021](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1111)). By capturing intricate temporal relationships, LSTMs not only enhance predictive accuracy but also address the unique challenges associated with forecasting in dynamic financial environments.

An analysis of the leading sources in this field underscores the rapid advancement of machine learning applications for financial forecasting, which has resulted in a significant research output. Key journals such as “Expert Systems with Applications”, “IEEE Access”, and “Computer Economics” are central to this discipline, collectively contributing a large volume of the literature. The prominence of these journals suggests that they are regarded as reputable sources for innovative research in financial data forecasting. The presence of publications from various disciplines—including computer science, engineering, artificial intelligence and finance—highlights the inherently interdisciplinary nature of this field. Our analysis further reveals that most documents are multi-authored, reflecting the collaborative approach that characterizes this research area. This cross-disciplinary engagement is essential, as financial forecasting requires a fusion of domain expertise from finance with advanced technical skills in machine learning and engineering. By integrating diverse perspectives and methodologies, this collaborative environment fosters innovation and enhances the robustness of predictive models. Moreover, the high citation rates observed across these publications suggest that the research is not only prolific but also impactful, as it is frequently referenced by other researchers to inform and advance their own work. The findings emphasize the value of interdisciplinary partnerships, which contribute to the continuous evolution of financial forecasting models and their alignment with real-world applications and market needs.

The implications of this study are significant for several key stakeholders. For researchers, the study provides a roadmap of the prevailing trends, influential authors, and preferred methodologies within the field of financial forecasting. By identifying the most commonly studied topics and techniques, we offer insights into the current state of research, which can help guide future inquiries. Furthermore, exploring alternative models and hybrid ones based on the LSTM architecture could yield even better results, enhancing the predictive power and adaptability of financial forecasting models ([Yang & Wang, 2022](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1131); [Wang et al., 2021](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1128); [Widiputra et al., 2021](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1129); [Chen et al., 2021](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1098); [Lu et al., 2020](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1113); [Chen et al., 2019](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1097); [Cao et al., 2019](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1095); [Zhang et al., 2019](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1137); [Sun et al., 2018](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1125)). Our analysis of collaboration patterns also highlights potential opportunities for partnerships, which could foster a more integrated and cohesive research community.

For investors, the findings are equally valuable. The robust forecasting capabilities of artificial neural networks, particularly LSTM architectures, have proven effective in capturing the dynamics of financial markets. Given their capacity to uncover complex temporal relationships, LSTM-based models serve as valuable tools for investors seeking to make informed decisions in an increasingly complex and volatile market environment. Continued exploration and refinement of LSTM-based models may further improve the accuracy and reliability of financial predictions, offering even greater strategic advantages. Moreover, for regulators, the insights gained from machine learning-based forecasting models can aid in understanding market trends and anomalies, facilitating the development of policies aimed at ensuring market stability and protecting investors. As these models evolve, their potential to provide real-time, actionable insights could become an invaluable resource for regulatory bodies, enabling a proactive approach to market oversight and intervention.

Building upon the strengths of LSTM-based models in financial forecasting, integrating sentiment analysis into these predictions presents an additional avenue for enhancing accuracy and depth. Sentiment analysis, especially when applied to financial news, social media, and other real-time data sources, can capture the emotional and psychological drivers behind market movements, which are often overlooked in traditional models. The use of deep learning techniques, such as BERT or GPT-based models, in sentiment analysis has already shown promise in other domains ([Abdullah & Ahmet, 2022](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1091); [Zhang et al., 2018](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1136); [Tang et al., 2015](#979-8-3693-8186-1.ch018.bits-pdf.xhtml#_idTextAnchor1126)), and applying these tools to financial forecasting could provide valuable insights into market sentiment and its impact on asset prices. By combining the power of LSTM for temporal pattern recognition with the ability of deep learning models to interpret sentiment, researchers and investors alike could develop more nuanced forecasting models that account not only for historical data but also for the emotional pulse of the market. This integration holds potential for improving predictive performance, especially in volatile markets where sentiment can play a decisive role in driving price movements.

Despite the strengths of this study, several limitations must be acknowledged. First, while we analyzed a broad dataset from multiple sources, the study relied heavily on documents available in English and from a limited set of academic databases. This focus may have led to the exclusion of relevant research published in other languages or in less widely indexed journals. Additionally, while our study provides a high-level overview of research trends, it does not delve into the specific applications or performance comparisons of different machine learning models. Future studies could build upon this work by conducting more granular analyses of specific forecasting techniques and their efficacy across various financial markets. Furthermore, while our analysis identified key authors and collaborative networks, a deeper examination of the nature and outcomes of these collaborations could provide more insight into the mechanisms that drive innovation in this field.

### 6\. CONCLUSION

The application of advanced deep learning techniques and AI tools has significantly enhanced the rigor and depth of our scientometric analysis in the field of financial forecasting. Techniques such as natural language processing and topic modeling enabled by powerful models like Sentence-BERT, BerTopic, BERT, ChatGPT, and PEGASUS, have allowed us to capture and analyze complex thematic patterns within a vast corpus of literature. These tools provide a nuanced understanding of the research landscape by efficiently categorizing topics, summarizing large volumes of text, and highlighting latent semantic relationships within documents. In particular, embeddings have facilitated the visualization of research clusters, while topic modeling has helped to identify and track emerging themes over time. By leveraging these AI-driven methods, we not only enhance the precision and comprehensiveness of our analysis but also pave the way for future scientometric studies in other domains. The integration of these technologies demonstrates the transformative potential of deep learning and AI in driving innovation and improving the insights derived from large-scale academic research assessments.

Future research can expand on this work by exploring other transformer-based models and techniques for bibliometric analysis. Additionally, integrating other scientific data sources, can provide a more holistic view of research trends and impact. As DL technology continues to evolve, its applications in bibliometric and scientometric analysis will undoubtedly expand, offering new opportunities for advancing scientific research.

In conclusion, this study underscores the importance of machine learning as a transformative tool in the field of financial forecasting. By offering a detailed scientometric analysis, we have highlighted the key trends, influential contributors, and prevalent methodologies that define this research area. Our findings reveal a vibrant and expanding field characterized by a high level of international collaboration and a strong focus on predictive accuracy.

For industries, the robust capabilities of machine learning models, particularly LSTM architectures, present significant opportunities for enhancing financial decision-making. These models excel in capturing intricate temporal patterns, making them highly effective in addressing market volatility and complexity. Additionally, integrating sentiment analysis into forecasting frameworks, as highlighted in this study, offers a more comprehensive approach by accounting for emotional and psychological market drivers. To maximize the impact of these technologies, organizations should prioritize adopting explainable AI (XAI) solutions that ensure transparency and accountability, thereby increasing trust in model outputs. Furthermore, fostering collaborations with academic institutions, as evidenced by the global research networks identified in this analysis, can help bridge the gap between theoretical advancements and practical applications. By embracing continuous learning and ethical AI practices, industries can harness the transformative potential of machine learning, securing a competitive edge in the rapidly evolving financial landscape.

# About the Contributors

Haojun Chen holds a Doctorate in Business Administration with a specialization in finance from the University of Manchester Alliance Business School and an MSc in Statistics from Colorado State University. His publications include research articles in prestigious financial journals and several textbooks on financial data science. Dr. Chen has also served as a reviewer and book editor for leading international academic journals and publishers. With extensive experience in hedge funds and the securities industry, Dr. Chen is a founding partner of BlackGold Inc., a global quantitative finance research company. He currently serves as an associate professor of finance at Guangzhou Huali College International School.

\*\*\*

Yunus Emre Akdogan received his PhD from Bursa Uludag University in 2023. His research focuses on applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced data-driven approaches to financial decision-making. He specializes in a wide range of topics, including investment and corporate finance, behavioral finance, and the transformative impacts of digital technologies. His expertise encompasses applications of financial artificial intelligence, financial technologies, algorithmic trading, big data analytics, social media insights, natural language processing, sentiment analysis, blockchain, and cryptocurrencies. Dr. Yunus Emre Akdogan is a faculty member in the Department of Business Management at Yozgat Bozok University.

Harishchander Anandaram completed a PhD in bioengineering, an M.Tech., and a B.Tech. in bioinformatics from the Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology, Chennai, in 2020, 2011, and 2009. In his bachelor’s and master’s theses, he worked on analyzing resistance in HIV protease inhibitors based on molecular mechanics and machine learning studies, a collaborative project with IIT Madras. In his PhD thesis, he worked on pharmacogenomics and miRNA-regulated networks in psoriasis, a collaborative project with Georgetown University, USA, JIPMER, India, CIBA, India, and ILS, India. His thesis illustrated a multi-disciplinary approach by combining computational biophysics and molecular biology machine learning. While doing a PhD, He had the opportunity to collaborate with international researchers and have publications in reputed international journals in bioinformatics and systems biology. He has received the prestigious “Young Scientist Award” from “The Melinda Gates Foundation” for his research abstract on “The Implications of miRNA Dynamics in Infectious Diseases”. To date, he has reviewed more than 200 manuscripts in systems biology.

Jay Arora is currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering and Technology with a specialization in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) from the Sharda School of Engineering and Technology, located at Sharda University, Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India. His academic journey reflects a deep curiosity in leveraging computing technologies to address real-world challenges and enhance efficiency across industries. Throughout his academic tenure, Mr. Jay has developed proficiency in foundational and advanced topics in Computer Science, including algorithms, data structures, databases, web technologies, and software development methodologies. This holistic academic experience has empowered him with the skills to understand and solve technical problems using innovative approaches. Apart from theoretical concepts, Mr. Jay has a hands-on approach toward learning, exemplified through various projects, practical assignments, and hackathon participations. His passion for programming is evident in his growing expertise in languages like Python, C++, JavaScript, and Java.

K. Balaji is an Assistant Professor in Business and Management, Christ University, Bangalore. He did Ph.D. from KLU Business School, KL University,Vijayawada. He is having 12 years of teaching experience. He has to his credit 23 Research Articles published in reputed National and International Journals. He has participated and presented more than 12 papers in both National and International Seminars/Conferences and also attended more than 50 workshops/FDPS organized by various reputed organizations. He has also participated in more than 50 seminars / webinars organized by various reputed organizations. He has also attended in 6 Short Term Training programs.He has successfully conducted 3 webinars, one 5 day FDP and one International Conference on Reimaging marketing in New Normal. He is a ratified as Assistant Professor by both JNTUH, JNTU Anantapur and Sri Venkateswara University,Tirupati. His specialized areas include, Accounting and Financial management, Marketing Management, Retailing Managemen

Imane Boudri, Doctor in Economics and Finance, is an Associate Professor in the Finance Department at ISCAE, Morocco, specializing in financial innovation and market analysis.

Simone Casciaro holds a Master’s degree in Computer Engineering and is currently a Ph.D. candidate in Complex Systems Engineering at the University of Salento (Italy). His current research focuses on One-Time Programs, with an emphasis on developing secure and efficient applications for this emerging computing paradigm. In addition to his primary research, Simone has a great interest in Green Software, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Fintech, and the applications of computer science within the fields of Medicine and Education. In 2024 he co-founded Snaproof Srl, an Italian startup which received funds from FoolFarm Spa, an AI startup factory with global coverage.

K. A. Dhanya is presently serving as Assistant Professor at School of Business Management, Christ University, Bangalore. She holds PhD in Commerce from University of Calicut, M Phil from Bharathiar University, M. Com from Calicut University and MBA from Madras University. She has also qualified UGC-NET and JRF in commerce in 2004. To her credit she has 15 publications in different national and international journals and 12 paper presentations in national and international conferences. She has been awarded with Minor Research Project sponsored by the UGC New Delhi in 2014. She has co -authored 2 books and edited 3 books. She has been Resource person in more than 10 seminars and conferences. She has a teaching experience of more than 16 years and has held various academic and administrative positions. She served as Head of the Department of Commerce and Management Studies, Amal College of Advanced studies, Nilambur Kerala during 2010- 2024. She has undertaken a social project in 2019 for revamping tribals in Nilambur Taluk. Due to her contributions in academia and society she has been awarded ‘Vanitha Rathna Puraskar’ by Jan Shikshan Sansthan Malappuram.

Ding Ding is the Dean of the School of Business at the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) where she has worked since 2008. She obtained her PhD in Economics from Nanyang Technological University and is a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA). She has taught various finance courses at the undergraduate, post-graduate, and executive training level. Her recent research focuses on the developments and applications of Financial Technology (FinTech), and she has developed courses to help students understand and adapt to the new digital economy.

Chong Guan is Associate Professor and Director at SUSS Academy, Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS), Singapore. Her research interests lie in the area of machine learning in business applications. Her publications appear in leading journals such as International Journal of Consumer Studies, Environmental Science and Pollution Research, Electronic Commerce Research, Electronic Markets, European Journal of Marketing, Journal of Interactive Marketing, Journal of Business Research and Telecommunications Policy. She is an editorial board member of Internet Research. She has consulted business practices and conducted corporate training on analytics, AI, FinTech and other emerging areas. She served as a member of Task Force 6 for Economy, Employment, and Education in the Digital Age at Think20 (T20) in 2020. She is the Chairperson for ACE PSEI Sub-Committee. Chong completed her Ph.D in Marketing at Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University, and her undergraduate studies in Marketing at Guanghua School of Management, Peking University, China.

Rajkumar Jagdale is an Assistant Professor and Head of the Department of Computer Science at the Faculty of Science and Technology, Vishwakarma University, Pune. He earned his Ph.D. in Computer Science and IT from Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University, Chh. Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, India. With over six years of teaching and research experience, complemented by two years in the industry as Data Scientist, Dr. Jagdale specializes in Sentiment Analysis, Opinion Mining, Text Mining, Machine Learning, Big Data Analytics, and RPA. He has made significant academic contributions, with 13 publications in reputable international journals and conferences, and holds one patent related to his research. Dr. Jagdale's work has received notable recognition, including prestigious scholarships such as the JASSO Scholarship to attend a Spring School on “Smart Materials and AI” at Tokushima University, Japan, and the DST Inspire Fellowship from the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India. Additionally, he was awarded a Gold Medal for his exemplary performance in the M.Sc. Computer Science program. He reviewed conference papers and journals and He is member of CSI, ISCA and IAENG.

Vishal Jain is presently working as an Associate Professor at Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Sharda School of Engineering and Technology, Sharda University, Greater Noida, U. P., India. Before that, he has worked for several years as an Associate Professor at Bharati Vidyapeeth’s Institute of Computer Applications and Management (BVICAM), New Delhi. He has more than 16 years of experience in the academics. He obtained Ph.D (CSE), M.Tech (CSE), MBA (HR), MCA, MCP and CCNA. He is life member of CSI, ISTE and senior member of IEEE. His research areas include information retrieval, semantic web, ontology engineering, data mining, ad hoc networks, and sensor networks.

Devapitchai Joel Jebadurai is working as an Associate Professor in the Department of MBA, St. Joseph's College of Engineering, OMR, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. He has published two books and more than 50 research articles in various peer-reviewed journals.

K. Dheenadhayalan working as an Assistant Professor in Department of MBA, Sri Sai Ram Engineering college, Chennai. He had a rich experience in the field of teaching.

Sachin Kaushik is a Assistant Professor in Department of Computer Application in HRIT University, Ghaziabad, U.P, India. He wrote a number of research papers and books.

Vineet Kaushik is a Professor and Dy. Dean in School of Commerce and Management in IIMT University, Meerut, U.P, India. He has an overall experience of around 22 year in academic, business and industry. He wrote a number of research papers and books.

Sathish Kumar M is an Assistant Professor in the Information Technology Department, Nehru Institute of Engineering and Technology, Coimbatore. Graduated M.E, Computer Science And Engineering, in SVS College of Engineering and Technology from Anna University, Chennai. Graduated B.E, in P.A College of Engineering and Technology from Anna University, Chennai. My research area interests include, Computer Networks, Cyber Security and Artificial Intelligence.

Luca Mainetti is a full professor of Software Engineering in the Department of Innovation Engineering at the University of Salento (Italy). His research interests include web design methodologies, notations and tools, web and services oriented architectures and applications, collaborative computer graphics. He is scientific coordinator of the GSA Lab – Graphics and Software Architectures Lab ([www.gsalab.unisalento.it](www.gsalab.unisalento.it)), and IDA Lab – Identification Atomation Lab ([www.idalab.unisalento.it](www.idalab.unisalento.it)). He is Rector’s delegate to ICT. Mainetti received a PhD in computer science from Politecnico di Milano (Italy), where he has been supply teacher of Hypermedia Applications and Human Computer Interaction, and he contributed to create the HOC (Hypermedia Open Center) laboratory. He is a member of the IEEE and ACM. He is author of more than 270 international scientific papers. Contact him at luca.mainetti@unisalento.it.

Shikha Malhotra is a PhD in Finance and has more than 11 years of experience, with 9 years in SBI as an officer and 2 years with a teaching experience. She is FRM Certified from GARP and CFA Level 2 passed (CFA US). She has two research publications in ABDC-B and ABDC-C.

Priyakrushna Mohanty (PK) is an Assistant Professor at the Department of Business and Management, Christ University, Bengaluru. Holding a Ph.D. in Tourism Studies from Pondicherry University, where he was a UGC Senior Research Fellow, Dr. Mohanty is a recipient of the prestigious Travel Corporation (India) Gold Medal for his Master's in Tourism Studies. His academic qualifications extend to an M.Com. in Finance and PG Diplomas in Rural Development, Research Methodology, and Teaching Skills. With prior industry experience at Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd., he brings a practical perspective to his role. A prolific researcher, Dr. Mohanty has authored over forty publications and co-edited five books with renowned publishers such as Routledge, Emerald, Springer Nature, and CABI. His research interests encompass Research Methodology, Tourism Sustainability, Livelihood, Events Tourism, e-Tourism, and Gender issues in Tourism Development.

P. Ashok is from Chennai, Tamilnadu. He is currently employed as Associate Professor at Symbiosis Institute of Digital and Telecom Management (SIDTM), affiliated to Symbiosis International (Deemed University), Pune from November 2022. His areas of interest include Optical/Wireless Communication, Telecom Regulations and Standards. He does active research in the field of Quantum Cascade Lasers where he has published high quality papers in reputed journals along with this research supervisor Dr. M. Ganesh Madhan from Madras Institute of Technology, Chennai. Other allied fields of interest include AI, ML, DS and modern-day technologies in Telecom networks. His ability to make complex things simple is his way of teaching. He also has 3 patents to his credit in the field of IoT. He has close to 71 high quality research articles indexed in Scopus and Web of Science databases.

Jing Ren is a Senior Lecturer at the School of Business, Singapore University of Social Sciences. She holds a PhD in Information Systems from Singapore Management University. Her research focuses on artificial intelligence, recommendation systems, UGC and fintech. She serves as an Associate Editor for the academic journals Electronic Commerce Research and Applications, Data Science and Management.

Vikas Sharma completed his Graduation and Post Graduation from Chaudhary Charan Singh University, Meerut, U.P. Currently Pursuing his Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from Govt. Recognized University. Presently, he is working as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Applications, IIMT University, Meerut, U.P. He has been awarded as Excellence in teaching award 2019. He is the reviewer member of some reputed journals. He has published several book chapters and research papers of national and international reputed journals.

Aniket Singh is a Assistant Professor in Department of Computer Science and Engineering in Delhi Technical Campus, Greater Noida, U.P India. He wrote a number of research papers and books.

Partap Singh is committed to teaching and research in Finance and Investment domain since last 18 years+. His qualification is PhD (Commerce), M. Com (Finance& Accounting), and MBA(Finance). He has rich work experience in the field of Teaching, administration and research as well. He held various responsibilities like Editor, Co-editor, and Editorial Board member, Associate Editor in number of national and international journals. He has regularly been receiving offers for writing books from the top publishing houses of India and received many letters of thanks& compliments for giving valuable suggestions and commendable views concerning improvement of many leading Publications/Books. He has written and published 5 books namely Financial Management, Risk Management, working capital Management, Management Accounting and Analysis of Financial Statements. Further, he has published more than 60 papers and book chapters in good reputed journals and he has also contributed numerous research papers in national and international conferences or seminars. He has good participation in MDPs. FDPs and STCs as well as Life Membership of reputed academic bodies. His future interest area of research is Financial Market, Financial Derivatives, Technological innovations in Finance& Investment, Artificial Intelligence and Its Impact on Finance and Investment. ” Dr Partap Singh is currently working as Professor, MMIM, Maharishi Markandeshwar (Deemed to be University) University, Mullana, Haryana, India.”

Dailin Song is a graduate student in Statistics at Columbia University. He has earned a bachelor’s degree in Data Science from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Dailin has been a recognized and active code contributor in the GitHub and StackOverflow communities.

Shashi Teotia is Assistant Professor in Department of Computer Application, Chaudhary Charan Singh University (Campus), Meerut. She constantly proved excellence in teaching and all academic work. She is having 15 Years teaching experience. She has handled many subjects for UG and PG students. She has supervised more than 100 projects PG Level. She has organized many Workshops, Seminars both International level and National level. She is expertise in Computer Network, Cloud Computing and Digital Electronics etc. She has published more than 15 research papers and articles in reputed journals. She has published 2 book and 2 book chapters. She has published 2 patents. She is reviewer and editor in many reputed journal and international conference. She has also been co-coordinator for college Affiliations like NAAC, AICTE etc. She has a member of Board of Studies in university Meerut. She is life time member of Computer Society of India and IAENG.

Aysel Varoglu holds a BS degree in Economics from Gazi University (2013) and an MA degree in Energy Economics and Management from Social Sciences University of Ankara (2022). She works on energy economics and analysis at the Ministry of Trade. She has published research articles and book chapters on the strategic and economic importance of energy and climate change. Her research interests are mainly in the macroeconomic impacts of energy and climate change.

Tarun Kumar Vashishth is an active academician and researcher in the field of computer science with 21 years of experience. He earned Ph.D. Mathematics degree specialized in Operations Research; served several academic positions such as HoD, Dy. Director, Academic Coordinator, Member Secretary of Department Research Committee, Assistant Center superintendent and Head Examiner in university examinations. He is involved in academic development and scholarly activities. He is member of International Association of Engineers, The Society of Digital Information and Wireless Communications, Global Professors Welfare Association, International Association of Academic plus Corporate (IAAC), Computer Science Teachers Association and Internet Society . His research interest includes Cloud Computing, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Operations Research; published more than 45 research articles with 2 book and 55 book chapters. He is contributing as member of editorial and reviewers boards in conferences and various computer journals published by CRC Press, Taylor and Francis, Springer, IGI global and other universities.

Roberto Vergallo is a Tenured Assistant Professor in the software engineering field. His current research topics include the design and development of innovative customer experience (CX) for the banking field using the innovation lead by recent advancements in AI, IoT and DLT. As a side research topic, he is contributing to the foundation of the sustainable software engineering field, particularly focusing on Green AI methods and techniques. He has authored more than 50 scientific papers published in international journals, conference proceedings, and books. In 2024 he has been a visiting researcher at TU Delft (The Netherlands) where he joined the Software Engineering Research Group (SERG), led by prof. Arie van Deursen, to contribute to the field of Green AI. In a previous position at University of Salento (Lecce, Italy) he has coordinated for 15 years the activities of the GSA-Lab, led by prof. Luca Mainetti. His PhD thesis (2014) was on a model-driven Cloud architecture for the IoT. It was the result of an experience at the prestigious UCLA (Los Angeles, CA), after which he moved back to Italy and founded a spin-off company called Vidyasoft srl. With the spin-off he raised 200k€ from the industry for the result of his research, as well as receiving different grants and awards from banks and financial institutions. In 2022-2023 he has worked closely with Bank of Italy, as he was admitted to both the MilanoHub program (AI for Fintech) and the first Italian Regulatory Sandbox. In 2023 he contributed to the public discussion on the Digital Euro project with the ECB by proposing his invention on an offline P2P payment protocol. He is member of the editorial board for three international journals: MDPI Fintech, Journal on Information and Communication technology (JICT), and Journal of Telecommunication, Electronic and Computer Engineering (JTEC). In 2024 he has been part of the organizational committee of the 10th Italian Conference on ICT for Smart Cities and Communities (I-CiTies), where he has been the national coordinator of the Smart City University Challenge.

Yu Yinghui is an associate professor with the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS). She obtained her PhD in Finance from University of Hong Kong and her research interests include asset pricing, alternative investments, risk management as well as financial technologies and innovations.
